Description: Detection limit, one per reported concentration variable (one per target species, these being the same set), with its units. For the procedure: the typical detection limits. For the session: the limits achieved in this session, where they are determined for the session as a whole (for example, from the blanks of the run). The calculation method is recorded separately in Detection Limit Method. Record 'N/A' where the procedure reports no concentrations. In the dataset: report the detection limit of each analysis, where the procedure computes one.
Formula or approach used to calculate the detection limits, with a citation for the method where one exists. Must be consistent with the values reported in Detection Limit.

How the uncertainty predicted from counting statistics — the theoretical limit set by the Poisson distribution of the counts accumulated — is computed for each reported quantity, and the sigma level it is quoted at. It is derived from the counts on the target species together with those on any background or blank subtracted from it. Distinct from the scatter actually observed within a measurement or between repeated measurements, which is recorded separately. In the dataset: report, for each analysis and reported quantity, the counting-statistics uncertainty at the stated sigma level.
Purpose: Where a procedure reports both, agreement indicates the measurement is shot-noise limited, and a larger observed scatter indicates a further source of variance.

Description: Every reference material or reference scale used in the procedure or session: calibration and bracketing standards, quality-control (secondary) materials, and materials used for interference or delta corrections. List each material once, whatever roles it holds; the fields that assign standards to target species name entries in this list.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., NIST SRM 612 | Kakanui kaersutite | San Carlos olivine | IRMM-014 | V-CDT | None
Purpose: A result can be checked only against the standards that produced it, and a material that serves several roles is one standard, not several.

Description: The kind of material each reference material is (mineral, glass, metal, solution, gas or reference scale), with the mineral or phase name where it has one.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., olivine | synthetic silicate glass | metal | single-element solution | reference scale
Purpose: A mismatch between a standard's matrix and the samples' is a common source of bias in microbeam and laser-ablation analysis.

Description: The registry or catalogue identifier of each reference material, where one exists: an IGSN, a certifying body's catalogue number (NIST, IRMM, USGS) or a museum catalogue number (USNM). Where the material is also registered as a sample, give the same identifier as in Sample Persistent Identifier. Record 'None' for an in-house material with no registered identifier.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., NIST SRM 612 | USNM 111312/444 | IRMM-014 | None
Purpose: Material names are reused across lots and suppliers; the identifier says which material was used.

Description: The publication, compilation or certificate giving the accepted values used for each reference material, with a DOI where available. Where values for different properties of one material come from different sources, say which applies to which.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., Jochum et al. 2011, doi:10.1111/j.1751-908X.2011.00120.x | GeoReM preferred values | certificate of analysis
Purpose: Results calibrated against different published values for the same material are not directly comparable.

Description: The accepted value of each reported property for each reference material, as a number with its unit. Its uncertainty is recorded in Reference Value Uncertainty and its source in Reference Value Source.
Purpose: Without the accepted value an accuracy figure can be read but not recomputed.

Description: The uncertainty of each accepted value in Reference Value, in the same unit, at the level stated in Reference Value Uncertainty Basis.
Purpose: An accuracy figure means something only against the uncertainty of the value it is measured against.

Description: What the uncertainty in Reference Value Uncertainty represents: its coverage and how it was obtained.
Purpose: The basis is the part most often left implicit, and the part an accuracy calculation depends on.

Description: Post-acquisition normalization applied to the reported data beyond the primary calibration — for example correction to a reference value derived from secondary reference materials, or correction for a systematic bias those materials reveal. Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.

The reference material against which each target species is calibrated in each target material, converting raw signal intensities to concentrations, or anchoring an isotope ratio as the bracketing standard. Name an entry in Reference Materials. Where calibration instead uses the vendor's stored library or theoretical response factors rather than measured reference materials — 'standardless' or 'semi-quantitative' quantification — record that here, naming the library or model used. 'None' means no calibration was performed at all, which is a different answer.
Purpose: Which standard calibrates which target species in which material decides whether the calibration is matrix-matched.

Description: The reference material(s) run as unknowns to check the results for each target species in each target material, assessing accuracy independently of the calibration and monitoring drift. Name one or more entries in Reference Materials.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., San Carlos olivine | BHVO-2, BCR-2 | NIST 612, BCR-2G
Purpose: Only a material that played no part in the calibration tests its accuracy.
